methodologyNotes: Roster covers 11 motorized baby swings/rockers plus one motor-free outlier (the Nuna LEAF grow) — 12 products total — from 4moms/UPPAbaby, Graco, Fisher-Price/Mattel, Ingenuity/Kids2, Munchkin, and Nuna. Data was independently re-verified via manufacturer/brand sites (uppababy.com, munchkin.com, kids2.com, m.service.mattel.com, nunababy.com, PR Newswire) and major retailer/marketplace listings (Target, GoodBuy Gear, PeppyParents, FromRebel) where the manufacturer site blocked automated access — gracobaby.com and cpsc.gov returned 403 bot-check errors on every WebFetch attempt, so Graco specs lean on Target/marketplace corroboration and the CPSC Snuga recall was confirmed through the public SaferProducts.gov recall API instead of a raw cpsc.gov fetch. weight_limit_lb is in pounds; power_source is plug_in/battery/both, except the Nuna LEAF grow, which is manually operated (no motor) and marked 'manual'. Boolean fields indicate simple presence/absence; recline_positions is a discrete count where a brand publishes one, else a descriptive range string (e.g. continuous 25°–45°). The Fisher-Price Sweet Snugapuppy Dreams entry (model DRG43) carries an active CPSC recall (recall #25009, announced Oct 10 2024, suffocation hazard, 5 deaths) — verified via SaferProducts.gov; see its provenance before treating it as a current buy. Corrections applied vs. the draft: removed three unsupported 'foldable:true' flags on fixed/non-folding units (mamaRoo, Snugapuppy cradle swing, Nuna LEAF), dropped the unsupported '(2.0)' RockaRoo label, nulled the Nuna release year (award year, not a verified release), nulled the unverifiable Graco Slim Spaces MSRP and replaced its broken Target-search source URL. accessedAt 2026-08-16.

products.name: 4moms mamaRoo Smart Swing (successor to mamaRoo 5.0)
products.priceNote: MSRP as listed by UPPAbaby/Target; this is the current 'Mamaroo Smart Swing' sold on uppababy.com, the continuation of the mamaRoo line.

specs.motion_types: 5 motions (car ride, kangaroo, tree swing, rock-a-bye, wave) via MultiMotion up-and-down + side-to-side blends

products.provenance: Price ($349.99), 25 lb weight limit, 5-motion/5-speed system, 25°–45° continuous recline, AC-only power (no batteries), and Bluetooth/Alexa/Google Home control all confirmed on UPPAbaby's official product page and cross-checked on Target's live listing (SKU A-95053957, $349.99). The mamaRoo line is now marketed and sold by UPPAbaby on uppababy.com; the acquisition mechanism was not independently verified and the brand is labeled '4moms (UPPAbaby)' accordingly. foldable was changed from the draft's 'true' to null — the mamaRoo Smart Swing is a fixed-base unit and neither UPPAbaby's nor Target's page states it folds. Exact relaunch/release date could not be confirmed and was left null.

products.name: Graco Sense2Soothe Swing with Cry Detection Technology
products.priceNote: MSRP ($249.99) confirmed via GoodBuy Gear listing, which shows the item marked down from a $249.99 retail price.

specs.motion_types: 8 motions incl. gentle sway, car ride, figure-eight, side-to-side and front-to-back; Cry Detection auto-adjusts motion/sound

products.provenance: 8 motions, 3 speeds, and a removable seat that doubles as a stand-alone rocker were confirmed on the GoodBuy Gear listing, which also shows the item marked down from a $249.99 retail price — upgrading the draft's 'directional estimate' to a corroborated MSRP. Weight range (5–30 lb), dual AC-adapter/4-D-battery power, and 3-position recline are drawn from the swing's own user manual (manua.ls). Direct WebFetch of gracobaby.com returned 403 bot-check on every attempt, so this entry relies on manual + marketplace evidence rather than a raw manufacturer fetch. foldable not published — left null.

products.name: Fisher-Price Sweet Snugapuppy Dreams Cradle 'n Swing (model DRG43)
products.priceNote: Historical price (~$160, per CPSC recall record) for the period it was sold (Oct 2010–Jan 2024). Not a current purchase price — discontinued and recalled.
products.provenance: SAFETY NOTE: this exact model (DRG43) is named in Fisher-Price's Snuga Swings recall — independently verified via the public SaferProducts.gov recall API: recall #25009, announced Oct 10 2024, ~2.1 million US units, covering all Snuga Swing models incl. DRG43 ('Sweet Snugapuppy'), sold Oct 2010–Jan 2024 for ~$160, after 5 infant suffocation deaths (2012–2022) in unsupervised sleep with added bedding. The /Recalls/2025/ URL reflects CPSC's fiscal-year-2025 numbering (FY25 begins Oct 2024), consistent with the Oct 2024 announcement. 6 speeds, 2 recline positions, 2 swing motions and AC/battery power confirmed directly on Mattel's DRG43 service page; ~$160 historical price and Oct 2010 sale start confirmed by the recall record. foldable changed from the draft's 'true' to null — this is a large stationary cradle 'n swing and folding is not stated on Mattel's page. Historical/discontinued/recalled — not a current buy recommendation.

products.priceNote: No current live MSRP could be independently confirmed for this exact model number on major retailers; left null rather than guessed.

products.priceNote: MSRP per 4moms' March 2023 PR Newswire release announcing the RockaRoo refresh.

products.name: Nuna LEAF grow
products.priceNote: Retailers show conflicting prices ($380 vs $575 for the toy-bar bundle) and Nuna's own US page is out-of-stock with no price shown, so priceUsd was left null.
products.provenance: Three recline positions, motor-free push-started motion (no batteries/cords), a detachable/washable seat that transitions to a toddler seat, and a Stage-2 capacity up to 130 lb were confirmed directly on Nuna's US product page, which showed the item out of stock with no price. releaseDate changed from the draft's '2019' to null — 2019 was the Red Dot Award year cited on the page, not a verified market-release date. foldable changed from 'true' to null — Nuna's page states the seat detaches from the base for storage but does not describe a fold-flat mechanism. This is a motor-free rocker, not a motorized swing — power_source is 'manual' as a deliberate deviation (see methodologyNotes).
